text:
sam: starting canary rollout of v2.8.0 to 10% (us-west + eu-west). watching p95 and errors.
deploy-bot: deploybot: canary rollout initiated for v2.8.0 -> 10% traffic. metrics tracked: p95_latency, error_rate, kvcache_miss_rate. autorevert=false.
maya: eu-west p95 is up ~30% vs baseline. kvcache miss_rate spike (~0.34) and kernel_fwd_time increased ~120ms in logs.
leo: any repro? can you share a sample query or affected customers?
maya: not deterministic, just telemetry from a handful of customers with long contexts; logs show increased evictions during their workloads.
sam: if kvcache misses are causing GPU kernel slowdown we could try warming prefixes but risky during canary. alternatives?
anne: confirm: autorevert is off so manual rollback required. need quick decision: rollback now or attempt mitigation?
paul: comms note: if we rollback, pin dedicated clusters to v2.7.9 and post an explanatory blurb for customers. I'll draft both internal and external messages.
leo: ops mitigation idea: temporarily cap max_seq_len to 1024 for canary traffic or reduce batching to lower kernel tail latency.
maya: capping seq_len worked in staging last week and cut kernel_fwd_time. can push routing rule for canary slice.
sam: propose plan: 1) short test: apply seq_len cap for 10m and watch; 2) if p95 remains >20% or error_rate rises, execute manual rollback to 2.7.9 and pin pools; 3) otherwise continue rollout with cap for 1h and file postmortem.
anne: agree with short test. prepping rollback checklist now so we can flip quickly. will include kubectl pin commands and the customer/internal blurbs Paul is drafting.
paul: internal blurb draft: "Pausing v2.8.0 rollout and reverting to v2.7.9 due to a performance regression impacting p95 latency for long-context requests. Investigating kvcache eviction patterns." customer blurb draft: "We've paused a performance update and reverted to the previous version while we investigate latency for long-context requests. No action required on your side." tagging legal for quick ack.
deploy-bot: deploybot: applying routing throttle: seq_len_max=1024 for v2.8.0 traffic slice in eu-west. will re-evaluate in 10m.
maya: telemetry tick: after the cap p95 trended down to +8% over baseline at 3m. kvcache miss rate decreased.
leo: promising. watch error budget closely but leaning to continue if stable at 10m.
sam: anne, finish rollback playbook (kubectl scale/pin commands, how to update dedicated routing, and release-note templates).
anne: done — checklist marked ready. pasted sample commands: `kubectl label nodes dedicated-pool=2.7.9 --overwrite` and `redwoodctl pool pin --pool=dedicated-eu-west --version=v2.7.9`. also added release-note snippets from Paul.
paul: prepping customer comms channel draft in #customer-communications-drafts. will post if we revert.
deploy-bot: deploybot: 8m update: eu-west p95 at +9% over baseline, error_rate unchanged. autorevert still disabled.
sam: hold until 10m mark. rollback if p95 >20% or errors spike. otherwise continue with seq_len cap for 1h and escalate to research for root cause.
leo: react with :thumbsup: if you approve the contingency (apply cap then rollback threshold).
maya: :thumbsup:
anne: :thumbsup:
paul: :thumbsup:
sam: :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deploybot: 10m canary check complete — condition met to continue restricted rollout (seq_len cap). no rollback performed.
paul: posting internal release note and marking rollback playbook "ready" for immediate use if needed later.
sam: follow-up: schedule a quick postmortem with research and kernel team to dig into kvcache eviction tuning and batching interactions.
leo: noted. I'll open a ticket and tag relevant owners.
paul: will update the release notes page with the mitigation steps and a link to the postmortem once available.
anne: closing thread until next metric update. keep alert channels notified.
